claims.gist: Technology leaders have more promising ideas than resources
A trend list is useful only if it guides funding decisions
These seven trends will most affect enterprise planning
Organizations need platforms to inventory, assess and govern AI
Treat AI governance as a funded operating function
Start with an inventory of all AI, including embedded
Synthetic media has made impersonation cheap
Fraud against executives and payment workflows is growing
Organizations will need identity and provenance verification tools
Remove approvals relying solely on voice or video identity
Defenders are shifting from detecting to preempting attacks
Shift security budget from alert handling to attack surface reduction
AI agents are moving from demonstrations to production
Agents bring risks of unintended actions and unclear accountability
Start agents narrow with minimal permissions and human checkpoints
General-purpose models are expensive and often imprecise on specialized work
Domain-specific models can deliver better accuracy at lower cost
Evaluate specialized models and invest in proprietary data
No single processing approach fits every workload
Avoid long commitments to one hardware architecture
AI energy demand has made power a strategic constraint
Customers and regulators want credible emissions data
Include energy and carbon costs; demand measured vendor figures
Do not act on all seven trends; apply a filter
Trends scoring high on relevance, readiness, risk deserve investment now
Revisit monitored trends in six months with a named owner
Technology choices are now inseparable from trust and accountability
Organizations planning early will move faster when technology matures

thesis: Seven 2027 trends across trust, intelligence and foundation; leaders should filter them by relevance, readiness and risk.
